name: Sao Tome and Principe Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Sign language; only refs are a 2014 dictionary and 2017 emergence papers — word stress inapplicable/undescribed

sources.citation: Moita, Mara; Abreu, Ana Maria; Mineiro, Ana. 2023. Iconicity in the emergence of a phonological system? Journal of Language Evolution 8(1): 1-17. doi:10.1093/jole/lzad009 (CC BY).
sources.note: Nothing. Read via the OUP HTML article page (PDF could not be reached by automated download; repositorio.ucp.pt copy hdl:10400.14/41863 refused connection). Analyses 200 signs at two time points 8 years apart for handshape, location, movement, palm orientation and non-manual expressions; finds handshape the parameter with the greatest development. No prosody, stress, rhythm or prominence content.

sources.citation: Mineiro, Ana; Báez-Montero, Inmaculada C; Moita, Mara; Galhano-Rodrigues, Isabel; Castro-Caldas, Alexandre. 2021. Disentangling pantomime from early sign in a new sign language: window into language evolution research. Frontiers in Psychology 12: 640057. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2021.640057.
sources.note: Nothing. Tracks use of head, torso and legs as articulators across four phases of LGSTP emergence (pantomime to conventionalised sign); no phonology or prosody section; the word 'stress' appears only in the sense of social pressure.

sources.citation: Mineiro, Ana; Carmo, Patrícia; Caroça, Cristina; Moita, Mara; Carvalho, Sara; Paço, João; Zaky, Ahmed. 2017. Emerging linguistic features of Sao Tome and Principe Sign Language. Sign Language & Linguistics 20(1): 109-128. doi:10.1075/sll.20.1.04min (author accepted manuscript, green OA via RUN/UNL hdl:10362/28979).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.2 'Phonological characteristics of emerging signs' (ms pp. 7-8) lists the manual parameters (handshape, orientation, movement, location), one- vs two-handed signs, an unconstrained location parameter, a very large signing space and heavy use of non-manuals and non-hand body articulators; Sec. 4.4 (ms pp. 10-11) treats facial expressions as adverbial and prosodic/syntactic markers (brow furrow + forward head tilt in interrogatives). No statement about word/sign-level stress or prominence.
